raw_response:
Well, I've been farming these 3 mu of land for near 50 years now, since I was a young man. At 70, my back isn't what it used to be, but I still know every inch of this plot. My son works over in the county town at a construction site, and my daughter-in-law is there too at a garment factory, so they send some money home. That helps with the grandchildren's schooling, but it also means there's fewer hands at planting and harvest time. My wife and I do most of the field work, though the grandchildren help during summer holiday.

This year, I'm sticking with cotton on all 3 mu. I've tried wheat-maize double cropping before, but at my age, the rush between wheat harvest and maize planting is too much — barely a week's time and you're running yourself ragged. Cotton is steadier. One planting, multiple pickings from September through October. Yes, it needs more labor for picking, but my daughter-in-law comes back for the harvest season, and we can manage.

I'll plant around April 20th, once the soil warms up proper. I saved some seed from last year — a local early-maturing variety that's done well for me. Buying new hybrid seed costs too much, and this seed is reliable. I'll put down about 10 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer before planting — that's what I've done for years. The soil here is decent but not rich. Maybe 12 kg of urea per mu for topdressing at flowering stage, split into two times if the plants look strong. I can't afford to go heavy on fertilizer like those big farms. Last year I used about 20 kg of nitrogen total per mu and got around 280 kg of lint per mu. That was fine. This year I'll do similar, maybe a touch less if fertilizer prices stayed high. My neighbor Old Wang said he cut back on fertilizer last year and his yield dropped, so I'm not taking that risk. Better to waste a little money than lose the crop.

For irrigation, I have the well, but pumping costs electricity. I'll irrigate twice — once at planting if it's dry, and once at peak flowering in July or August if the rain doesn't come. Cotton doesn't like wet feet, so I'm careful not to over-water. Flood irrigation is what I have.

Pesticides are a must for cotton. Bollworms will eat you alive if you don't spray. I'll do 3 or 4 sprays — herbicide before planting, then insecticide 2 or 3 times during the season if I see worms. I buy the generic brands from the supply shop in town. They're cheaper and work fine.

For tillage, I'll plow once with the small tiller I have, then harrow before planting. Nothing fancy. Labor is mostly my wife and me for the regular work — maybe 25 family days total across the season. For picking, I'll hire 2 or 3 local women for about 5 days total at 80 yuan per day each. My hands are too slow now for all that picking, and the grandchildren have school.

I expect about 270-280 kg of lint per mu this year if the weather holds. Last year was decent, no big disasters. You never know with the weather, but I've seen worse. Total input cost should be around 1,800 to 2,000 yuan for the 3 mu. That's about what I can manage without borrowing.
